items.q: Match the following pancreatic disease to its diabetes risk — 1) Chronic pancreatitis 2) Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma 3) Cystic fibrosis 4) Haemochromatosis … A) Most common cause of type 3c diabetes B) New-onset diabetes can be a presenting feature C) CFRD with insulin deficiency D) Iron deposition causing β-cell loss
items.exp: Chronic pancreatitis is the most common cause of type 3c; pancreatic cancer can present with new-onset diabetes; cystic fibrosis causes CFRD; haemochromatosis deposits iron in β-cells. (Book p925)

items.q: A 65-year-old with new-onset diabetes has weight loss and epigastric pain; CT shows a pancreatic mass. The most consistent interpretation is:
opts: New-onset diabetes as a presenting sign of pancreatic cancer
Type 2 diabetes with weight loss from low calorie diet
items.exp: New-onset diabetes with weight loss and pancreatic mass raises suspicion for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. (Book p925)

items.q: Assess type 3c: I Insulin therapy is usually required. II Metformin is the preferred first-line therapy in type 3c.
items.exp: Type 3c diabetes usually requires insulin because of combined endocrine and exocrine deficiency; metformin is not first-line. (Book p925)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a drug that causes hyperglycaemia?
items.exp: Metformin is hypoglycaemic; glucocorticoids, tacrolimus and olanzapine cause hyperglycaemia. (Book p925)

items.q: New-onset diabetes after solid-organ transplantation is most commonly caused by ___ therapy.
items.exp: Calcineurin inhibitors, especially tacrolimus, are common causes of post-transplant diabetes. (Book p925)

items.q: Match the following antibody result to its subtype on the page's algorithm — 1) High antibodies 2) Low antibodies 3) No antibodies … A) T1DM B) LADA C) T2DM or MODY
items.exp: The algorithm maps high antibodies to T1DM, low antibodies to LADA and no antibodies to T2DM or MODY. (Book p925)

items.q: A 45-year-old non-obese patient has high GAD antibody titre and progresses to insulin within 2 years. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Slow autoimmune progression in non-obese adult fits LADA. (Book p925)

items.q: Assess this caveat: I The page's algorithm labels 'Low antibodies' as T1DM and 'High antibodies' as LADA. II The C-peptide table on p928 reverses these patterns.
items.exp: The page's arrow scheme appears inverted (high antibody → T1DM, low → LADA); the C-peptide table on p928 uses the standard pattern (T1DM low C-peptide, LADA intermediate). Note this inconsistency when teaching. (Book p925)

items.q: Match the following drug to its diabetogenic mechanism — 1) Glucocorticoids 2) Olanzapine 3) Tacrolimus 4) Pentamidine … A) Increase gluconeogenesis and IR B) Weight gain and IR via H1 antagonism C) Direct β-cell toxicity D) β-cell destruction causing hypoglycaemia then diabetes
items.exp: Steroids drive gluconeogenesis and insulin resistance; olanzapine causes weight gain and IR via histamine antagonism; tacrolimus has direct β-cell effects; pentamidine causes β-cell destruction with biphasic glycaemia. (Book p925)

items.q: A patient with Cushing disease has worsening diabetes despite escalating metformin. The most appropriate next step is:
items.exp: Treating the underlying hypercortisolism is essential; insulin is often needed regardless until cortisol is controlled. (Book p925)

items.q: Pentamidine is associated with ___ glycaemia initially, then diabetes.
items.exp: Pentamidine initially causes hypoglycaemia through β-cell destruction, followed by diabetes. (Book p925)

items.q: Assess these diabetogenic drugs: I Protease inhibitors can cause insulin resistance. II Niacin causes hyperglycaemia.
items.exp: Protease inhibitors (especially indinavir) cause insulin resistance; niacin also worsens glycaemia. (Book p925)
